text:
viv: quick thought for RFC follow-up: instead of per-chunk checksums, what if we provide a tiny signed merkle-root sidecar for a shard plus a very short "open-record" (first 1-2 windows) inline header so clients can safely start KV warmup and verify incrementally with a merkle proof fetched later?

anya: I like merkle since proof sizes are logarithmic. open-record avoids waiting for any extra fetch for the very first bytes. how would proof fetch interact with streaming?

marc: flow: 1) server advertises X-Weight-Open: base64(open-record) and X-Weight-Merkle-URL. 2) client streams weights and fills provisional KV for first windows. 3) client fetches merkle proofs for ranges in parallel. 4) promote provisional windows once proofs validate root_sig.

olga: two practical notes: a) merkle tree construction must be deterministic across packers (we have multiple artifact builders). need canonical chunking rules (chunk-size, pad, endianness). b) proof fetches are many small requests; better to have a compact batched proofs object to reduce roundtrips (e.g., proofs.tar or proofs.car).

artifact-bot: new signer v3 supports detached merkle roots: artifact.merkle.sig. Docs: https://artifacts.internal/docs/merkle-signing

viv: canonicalization noted. propose chunk-size default 1MB to keep tree depth small and proof count manageable. batch proofs into a sidecar proofs.car content-addressed blob. sidecar layout: {v:1, chunk_size, root_hash, proof_blob_url, open_record_base64, sig}.

marc: integration with safetensors: nothing changes on-disk; sidecars are external. but loaders that mmap must still be able to treat cached provisional ranges safely. we need API semantics for provisional entries: tombstone/unpin + atomic promote that can take a list of keys and a root_hash.

anya: runtime contract: - warmup.put(key, data, provisional=true) - runtime records provenance pointer (shard_id, chunk_idx) for each provisional entry - promote(list_of_keys, root_hash, sig) verifies proofs and flips provisional=false atomically - on verification failure, runtime tombstones those keys and schedules a refetch/fallback.

olga: question: what about partial verification—if some proofs validate and some fail? should we allow partial promote?

viv: I'd prefer an all-or-nothing per-promote call to keep semantics simpler. Promote batches by granularity (e.g., per-window group). If a batch fails, tombstone the batch and try fallback for that range.

marc: another thought: for delta-updates we can have chained merkle roots where a delta carries a small patch-set proofs that reference base-root; verification becomes verifying base-root + patch proofs. lets us stream-apply patches with proofs.

anya: security: require root_sig before any automatic promotion for non-dev fleets. For low-trust edge fleets we can allow unsigned open-records but mark provisional and set a short TTL. server header X-Weight-Trust: strict|lenient.

olga: perf: computing merkle proofs on the server for every shard push can be expensive for huge models. batch offline at artifact publish time and store proofs.car in artifact store. runtime only fetches proofs.car when needed.

artifact-bot: scheduled canary: eng-ml/merkle-warmup @ 06:00 UTC. Use proofs.car for canary models.

viv: good. I'll draft the RFC with the sidecar schema, canonical chunk rules, and runtime API changes. will include a minimal example header and a sample promote pseudo-API. example header: \n\nX-Weight-Open: eyJ2IjoiMSIsImRhdGEiOiJvcGVuLXJlY29yZCIsIm9mZiI6MH0=\nX-Weight-Merkle-URL: https://obj/models/m1/shard-000.proofs.car\n

anya: include metrics we need: provisional_promote_success_rate, proofs_fetch_rtt_ms, promote_batch_size, fallback_refetchs. Also tests for mmap loader compatibility and proofs.car retrieval via CDN.

marc: also add a small e2e test: stream first 4MB, attempt promote with proofs.car, then run a short inference trace to assert no provisional hits served for strict route.

olga: +1. anything else? consider adding a compact bloom in the open-record to hint which windows are worth prioritizing (hot windows) so we don't fetch proofs for unneeded windows early.

viv: nice micro-optimization. I'll add bloom-optional in schema. Thanks team, RFC incoming. :rocket:
